'''Jean-Louis Le Mouël''' (29 July 1938<ref>[https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/remungol-56500/jean-louis-le-mouel-une-vie-passee-etudier-le-geomagnetisme-2869689 Jean-Louis Le Mouël, une vie passée à étudier le géomagnétisme] {{in lang|fr}}</ref> – 24 September 2025) was a French [[Geophysics|geophysicist]] who was researcher at the [[Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris]] (IPGP), which he chaired, and member of the French Academy of sciences since 1988.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whoswho.fr/bio/jean-louis-le-mouel_26799|title=Who's who}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Le Mouël published numerous articles in academic journals, in particular with [[Vincent Courtillot]]. He is a recognized specialist in [[Earth's magnetic field|geomagnetism]]. His work in this field earned him the John Adam Fleming Medal in 1997.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wikiberal.org/wiki/Jean-Louis_Le_Mou%C3%ABl#cite_note-2|title=John Adam Fleming Medal}}</ref> He was a member of the [[American Geophysical Union]] and the [[Royal Astronomical Society]], a former president of the [[Société géologique de France|Geological Society of France]], and has received numerous scientific and non-scientific decorations. Officer of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'Honneur]], [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 1984, he also received the Grand Prix from the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|French Atomic Energy Commission]] in 1987 and the Petrus-Peregrinus Medal from the [[European Geosciences Union]] in 2004.

He questioned the importance of human influence on global warming. Le Mouël declared in 2009:<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wikiberal.org/wiki/Jean-Louis_Le_Mou%C3%ABl#cite_note-3 |title=Jean-Louis Le Mouël - Wikiberal |website=www.wikiberal.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213095919/http://www.wikiberal.org/wiki/Jean-Louis_Le_Mou%C3%ABl |archive-date=13 December 2009}}</ref>

"''The climate has varied greatly over the centuries and years. Is the recent warming due solely to human activity and the [[Greenhouse gas emissions|production of greenhouse gases]]? In view of the available observations, man-made global warming is only a hypothesis, which should be considered and discussed as such. Similarly, the consequences that are drawn from it should be discussed calmly''".

Le Mouël therefore called for a dispassionate scientific debate. For him, it is essentially solar activity that impacts the climate, as well as the Earth's magnetism.

Le Mouël died on 24 September 2025, at the age of 87.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Passing of Jean-Louis Le Mouël (1938–2025) |url=https://www.ipgp.fr/en/news-and-agenda/news/passing-of-jean-louis-le-mouel-1938-2025/ |access-date=2 July 2026 |website=www.ipgp.fr |language=EN}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* 1971, "Aeromagnetic Survey Of South-Western Europe Aeromagnetic Survey Of South-Western Europe", [[Earth and Planetary Science Letters|Earth and planetary science letters]] 12, with Eugène Le Borgne and Xavier Le Pichon
* V. Courtillot, J. Ducruix, J.l. Le Mouel, "Sur une accélération récente de la variation séculaire du champ magnétique terrestre", C.R.Acad.Sci.Paris, D287, 1095-1098 (1978)
* V. Courtillot, A. Galdeano, J.l. Le Mouel, "Propagation of an accreting plate boundary : discussion of a new aeromagnetic survey of the Republic of Djibouti", Earth Planet. Sci. Lett., 47, 144-160 (1980)
* " Le globe ", Jean-Louis Le Mouël, [[Xavier Le Pichon]], Claude Japart, in Université de tous les savoirs, T15, Odile Jacob, 05/2002
* 2007, "Are there connections between Earth's magnetic field and climate?", Earth Planet. Sci. Lett., 253, 328–339, with Vincent Courtillot
